anomalies.observed: R62 is valued "24k" in the netlist and SPICE deck, but its own description ("62.5mW ... 24Ω 0805"), its LCSC part (C2930261) and its MPN (FRC0805J240TSD, a 24Ω part) all specify 24 ohms. The value field and the part metadata disagree by three orders of magnitude.
anomalies.expected: R62 should be a 24 Ω resistor, consistent with the orderable part and description, unless 24 kΩ was intended and the MPN/description are wrong.

evidence.quote: (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If the 24 Ω part is what gets built, the 24 kΩ intent is wrong, or the reverse. Either way the resistor across VOUTN/VOUTP would be off by a factor of 1000, changing the current in this bias network.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of D17, D32 and D49 are all on /NET0037, and no other component pin is on that net. The anodes have no supply connection, unlike every other LED anode on the board (e.g. D8 and D10 on +3V3, D45 via R64 to +3V3). Their cathodes drive CM4 status outputs through series resistors.
anomalies.expected: The LED anode net should connect to the +3V3 supply so that the status LEDs (Ethernet and PI activity) can light when their cathode outputs are pulled low.
anomalies.impact: The three status LEDs (Ethernet nLED2, nLED3 and PI activity indicator) would never light, so link and activity status would not be visible on the board.

anomalies.observed: In the LTC4412 ideal-diode circuit, Q6's source (pin 2) is on +5V, the LTC4412 SENSE pin, and its drain (pin 3) is on NET0110, which is also the LTC4412 VIN pin and the USB VBUS net. The P-channel body diode therefore conducts from +5V toward VBUS, the reverse of the intended USB-to-+5V path.
anomalies.expected: For LTC4412 power-path OR-ing, the P-FET source should be on the input (VIN/VBUS) and its drain on the load (+5V, with SENSE on the load side). The stated purpose is reverse-current protection from the USB input.
anomalies.impact: The USB power path may not block reverse current as intended, and the +5V rail can back-feed the USB VBUS net. This matches the notes' statement that the USB power arrangement "doesn't work".

parsed.summary: The netlist shows a resistor whose value (24k) contradicts its own 24Ω description and MPN, and two other suspicious points: three status-LED anodes that are not connected to any supply, and a reversed P-FET in the LTC4412 USB power path. The value mismatch is the strongest evidence; the other two are plausible but less certain.
